title: AP Precalculus 2.4 — Exponential Function Manipulation Practice
question: Ten practice rewrites: turn a shift into a factor, change the base, and handle negative and fractional exponents.
intro:
**Quick recap:**

- Product property:

\[
b^{x+k}=b^k\cdot b^x
\]

- Power property:

\[
b^{cx}=\left(b^c\right)^x
\]

- Negative exponent:

\[
b^{-n}=\frac{1}{b^n}
\]

- Fractional exponent:

\[
b^{1/k}=\sqrt[k]{b}
\]

**Show your calculation before choosing A–D.**

questions.prompt:
Rewrite with a single base and exponent \(x\):

\[
27^{x/3}

questions.solution_title: Take the cube root of the base

questions.title: Root, then power
questions.prompt:
Rewrite with a single base and exponent \(x\):

\[
16^{3x/4}
\]
questions.solution:
\[
\begin{aligned}
16^{3x/4} &= \left(16^{3/4}\right)^x \\
16^{3/4} &= \left(16^{1/4}\right)^3 \\
&= 2^3 \\
&= 8
\end{aligned}
\]

So

\[
16^{3x/4}=\boxed{8^x}
\]

- Not \(12^x\): that multiplies \(16\) by \(\tfrac34\) instead of raising \(16\) to the power \(\tfrac34\).

questions.title: Fifth root, then square
questions.prompt:
Rewrite with a single base and exponent \(x\):

\[
32^{2x/5}
\]
questions.solution:
\[
\begin{aligned}
32^{2x/5} &= \left(32^{2/5}\right)^x \\
32^{2/5} &= \left(32^{1/5}\right)^2 \\
&= 2^2 \\
&= 4
\end{aligned}
\]

So

\[
32^{2x/5}=\boxed{4^x}
\]

- Not \(2^x\): it takes the fifth root of \(32\) but forgets the square.

questions.title: Negative exponent and root
questions.prompt:
Rewrite with a single base and exponent \(x\):

\[
9^{-x/2}
\]
questions.solution:
\[
\begin{aligned}
9^{-x/2} &= \left(9^{-1/2}\right)^x \\
9^{-1/2} &= \frac{1}{9^{1/2}} \\
&= \frac13
\end{aligned}
\]

So

\[
9^{-x/2}=\boxed{\left(\frac13\right)^x}
\]

- Not \(3^x\): it drops the minus sign, so it grows where the function decays.

questions.title: Exponential in the denominator
questions.solution_title: Move the power up: the exponent changes sign
questions.solution:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{12}{3^{x-1}} &= 12\cdot3^{-(x-1)} \\
&= 12\cdot3^{1-x} \\
&= 12\cdot3\cdot3^{-x} \\
&= \boxed{36\left(\frac13\right)^x}
\end{aligned}
\]

- Check \(x=1\): the original gives \(\dfrac{12}{3^0}\), which is \(12\).
- The answer gives \(36\cdot\dfrac13\), which is also \(12\).
- Not \(4\left(\frac13\right)^x\): dividing by \(3^{-1}\) multiplies by \(3\), it does not divide.
